title: Symmetry — Imperfect Pairing
subtitle: Paired actions that align at onset and diverge in outcome
lineage: Lineage: Everynone, Symmetry (2011), commissioned with WNYC Radiolab
theorem: Create a paired image that first satisfies an expectation of correspondence, then reveals a difference consequential enough to alter the relation. Similarity directs attention toward particular lives.
boundary_note: Split-screen pairs do not imply simultaneous recording or personal acquaintance. Includes a sequential-cut alternative at the close to test which relations require simultaneity.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #04 (t=21.50s-30.50s): Right panel of the split-screen (`5444f8ed`) contains four rapid internal montage cuts instead of a continuous shot of chair movement.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: In Pair 3 (Seg #04), the right panel shatters split-screen comparison by cycling through four rapid internal montage cuts from the source reel instead of holding a continuous action against the left panel's waiting figure.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: Unverified internal source cuts inside `5444f8ed` (`Coffee House Rendezvous`, 1969) where a fast montage sequence was extracted as a single 9-second window.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Replace the right panel of Seg #04 with verified cut-free conference-table chair interaction `79565922` (10.5s-19.5s, 18.5s clean window) so the divergence against `91390311` is readable across the full 9-second hold.
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: Pair 1 (`cc7da646` vs `2df1341e`), Pair 2 (`31a9beb1` vs `473dcfbb`), and the Sequential-Cut Alternative proving why split-screen simultaneity is required.
